Article 17
(1) The Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various actions:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
(2) Every form of threatening action as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, whether carried out verbally or non-verbally, that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel that their life or safety is threatened, is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(3) Every form of Discrimination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b that is carried out and leads to gender, racial, or equality-based injustice, thereby degrading the status, freedom, and opportunities of women, is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(4) Every form of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c that is carried out in the form of physical, psychological, or sexual violence, thereby causing trauma to women, is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
(5) Every form of Exploitation as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d that is carried out in any form that degrades the dignity, worth, and honor of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

Article 19
(1) Social safeguarding as referred to in Article 18 letter a shall be carried out by the Regional Government together with the Village/Urban Village Government, the Business Sector, and the community.
(2) Social safeguarding as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be carried out by means of:
a. reporting if there is information on the occurrence of acts threatening Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against women;
b. implementing protection for Women Victims of acts threatening Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation;
c. conducting assistance and empowerment for Women Victims of acts threatening Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation; and/or
d. conducting safeguarding measures against perpetrators of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against Women who potentially endanger life safety.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. 6. Village is a village and customary village or called by other names, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage governmental affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency. 7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by other names who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration. 8. Urban Village (Kelurahan) is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus. 9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or gender-based discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life. 10. Child Victim is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life. 11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 12. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without using means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or forced services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trustworthy namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions. 17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence thereof against Women and Children. 18. Services is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which include complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives. 20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services. 21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems. 22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels. 23.

Article 25
(1) Physical and psychological health for Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation is intended to reduce and treat physical and psychological trauma.
(2) FKPP facilitates or carries out assistance/accompaniment or handling of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation.

Article 32
(1) The Regional Government together with the Village Government, the community, and the Business Sector shall carry out social safeguarding.
(2) Social safeguarding as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. reporting if there is information on Violence, Exploitation, neglect and/or Mistreatment Against Children;
b. protection of child witnesses and Child Victims by separating them from perpetrators in temporary care facilities;
c. assistance to Child Victims; and
d. securing perpetrators of violence who potentially endanger the safety of life.

Article 3
The implementation of protection for women and children is intended to provide a legal basis in implementing the protection of women and children in an integrated and comprehensive manner as well as to realize synergy between the Regional Government and the community in protecting women and children as vulnerable groups who are susceptible to becoming victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Mistreatment and/or neglect towards a Women-Friendly and Child-Appropriate Regency.

Article 38
(1) Child Victims of acts of Violence, Exploitation, Mistreatment of Children, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo rehabilitation in stages both physically, psychologically, and socially.
(2) Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall guarantee the living needs of Child Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) during the rehabilitation process.
(4) During the rehabilitation process, the provision of food intake, education, play activities, and appreciation for children who experience trauma as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to age and developmental needs.

Article 26
(1) Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process both physically, psychologically, and socially.
(2) Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of living needs of Female Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, mistreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

1.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines victims and violence broadly (Pasal 1 angka 9 and 14), including that violence can occur in the public sphere or “ranah kehidupan pribadi” (private/personal life). However, nowhere does it explicitly mention or define “kekerasan dalam rumah tangga” (domestic violence/KDRT) or violence by an intimate partner/household member as a distinct category. The judge inferred that ‘personal life’ implicitly equals domestic violence and answered Yes, but the indicator appears to require explicit domestic violence coverage. Since the retrieved English passages accurately reflect the Indonesian text and do not explicitly mention domestic violence, the error is the judge’s over-lenient inference rather than translation or retrieval.

1.5.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions women may suffer economically and defines exploitation broadly, the provided sentences do not explicitly identify economic violence/economic exploitation/domestic neglect as a specific form of violence against women (the violence clause lists physical, psychological, and sexual violence only).

1.5.rationale: The Indonesian text does cover economic harm/violence concepts. Pasal 1 angka 9 defines “Perempuan Korban” as suffering physical, psychological, sexual, economic, social losses (“kerugian… ekonomi”) due to violence/exploitation/discrimination. Pasal 1 angka 15 defines “Eksploitasi” to include forced labor/services and using someone’s labor/ability for material benefit (“mendapatkan keuntungan baik materiil maupun immaterial”), which is a form of economic exploitation. Pasal 8 ayat (2) huruf e and its official explanation also discuss protection of victims’ property/wealth with economic value (“harta… nilai ekonomis”). These points were present in the retrieved candidates (Article 1 definitions; Article 8 explanation). The judge focused narrowly on Pasal 17(4) listing physical/psychological/sexual violence and concluded there was no economic violence, ignoring the broader definitions and economic-loss language that supports a Yes label. So the information was available; the reasoning was too strict.

5.2.rationale: In the Indonesian source, there is no stakeholder-engagement requirement or mechanism specifically involving religious institutions/leaders (e.g., Kemenag, MUI, churches, pesantren, tokoh agama) in planning/implementation. The cited basis—Pasal 33 ayat (2) huruf d (“penyediaan Pendamping di bidang mental spiritual keagamaan”)—only states that services may include spiritual/religious counseling/assistance for child victims. That is a type of service content, not evidence of engaging religious stakeholders as partners/actors in governance or program delivery. The retrieved English passage matches the Indonesian meaning; the judge over-interpreted “religious matters” as “engagement of faith-related actors.” Therefore the discrepancy is due to evaluation failure, not translation or retrieval.
